subproblems.title: A unit orientation of a subspace has operator norm at most 1
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P (Euclid P), and let ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P n, i.e. a continuous linear functional on the normed space Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P (operator norms throughout). If ξ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q: there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P spanning Q such that ξ(α) = α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α), then ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (ξ : MultiVector P n), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (not part of the proof): this is the comparator-accepted DAG node `root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.imrep_measure_unique-a1.orientation_norm_bound-a1` (status accepted, candidate commit 0325970d8b47, isolated comparator passed) with a byte-identical frozen type, so the controller attaches it and creates no new work. The numbered proof below is that node's frozen parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim from its parent-child-handoff.json without the Lean implementation note. In it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of `root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.imrep_measure_unique-a1` (representation independence of θHⁿ⌞M, Simon 6.3.2(3)), and 'sibling K' names the sibling with key K here. Role here: the bound ‖ξ(y)‖ ≤ 1 in step 3 (the domination in the differentiation under the integral sign). It is used by scaled_derivative.

Source: step 1(c) of the parent proof of representation independence of θH^n⌞M (Simon Ch. 6, 3.2(3)): for an orthonormal family τ and any n-covector α, |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖; hence every unit orientation of an n-plane has norm at most 1. Norms: Covector (Euclid P) n = continuous alternating n-linear forms with the operator norm, MultiVector P n = its continuous dual with the operator norm.

1. By the hypothesis IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q choose an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1,…,τ_n) in ℝ^P (spanning Q; the spanning property is not used below) such that either ξ(α) = α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1,…,τ_n) for every n-covector α.
2. Fix an n-covector α. Since α is a continuous multilinear map, |α(τ_1,…,τ_n)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_{i=1}^n ‖τ_i‖ (operator-norm bound, Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). Orthonormality gives ‖τ_i‖ = 1 for every i, so the product is 1 (for n = 0 it is the empty product 1). Hence |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖.
3. In either sign case of step 1, |ξ(α)| = |±α(τ)| = |α(τ)| ≤ 1·‖α‖.
4. Step 3 holds for every n-covector α and 1 ≥ 0, so by the defining property of the operator norm of the continuous linear functional ξ (Mathlib ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound) we obtain ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1. ∎
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsUnitOrientationOf: ξ(α) = ±α(τ) for an orthonormal family τ.
|α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏‖τ_i‖ = ‖α‖ by the multilinear operator-norm bound and ‖τ_i‖ = 1.
Hence |ξ(α)| ≤ 1·‖α‖ for all α, so ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 by the operator-norm bound (opNorm_le_bound).

subproblems.title: Radial tangency gives x ∧ C⃗ = 0 a.e. (Simon 7.3.1 proof)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^P and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(U, n) such that p_x(x) = x for R.measure-a.e. x, where p_x is the orthogonal projection onto approxTangentPlane n M x. Then for R.measure-a.e. x and every (n+1)-covector β on ℝ^P, ξ(x)(ι_xβ) = 0. Here ι_xβ = ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x is the n-covector (v₁,…,vₙ) ↦ β(x, v₁, …, vₙ). This is Simon's 'x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e.'.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U : Set (Euclid P)) (R : IMRep U n), (∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, (approxTangentPlane n R.carrier x).starProjection x = x) → ∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), R.orient x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (not part of the proof): this is the comparator-accepted DAG node `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.wedge_vanishes-a1` (status accepted, candidate commit 9203aee8c87c, isolated comparator passed) with a byte-identical frozen type, so the controller attaches it and creates no new work. The numbered proof below is that node's frozen parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim from its parent-child-handoff.json without the Lean implementation note. In it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1` (constant density ratio implies cone, Simon 7.3.1), and 'sibling K' names the sibling with key K here. Role here: step 2. Applied with U = univ to R and the radial-tangency hypothesis, it gives ξ(x)(β.curryLeft x) = 0 for R.measure-a.e. x and every (n+1)-covector β.

Sources.
- Proof of Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt lines 358–359): "That is x ∈ T_x spt C for μ_C-a.e. x, so in particular x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e." This is step 5 of the parent proof.
- Simon Ch. 6, 3.1 (chapter-06.txt lines 733–742): ξ(x) = τ₁∧⋯∧τₙ for an orthonormal basis τ of T_xM.

Notation. M = R.carrier, ξ = R.orient, μ = R.measure. T_x = approxTangentPlane n M x and p_x is its starProjection. ι_xβ := ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x, so (ι_xβ)(v_1, …, v_n) = β(x, v_1, …, v_n).

1. Choosing good points. μ = (Hⁿ⌞M).withDensity θ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M, so the Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. property `orients` also holds μ-a.e. Together with the hypothesis: for μ-a.e. x there is Q with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q, and also p_x x = x. Fix such an x and an (n+1)-covector β.

2. x ∈ Q. The `if` in approxTangentPlane is satisfied (witness Q). The chosen subspace Q' satisfies HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt n M x Q', and HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique gives Q' = Q. So T_x = Q and p_Q x = x. An orthogonal projection fixes exactly the vectors of its range (Submodule.starProjection_eq_self_iff), so x ∈ Q.

3. Orientation data. IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q means: there is an orthonormal τ : Fin n → ℝ^P with span(range τ) = Q, and either ξ(x)(α) = α(τ) for all α, or ξ(x)(α) = −α(τ) for all α.

4. Vanishing on Q.
- The map y ↦ (ι_yβ)(τ) = β(y, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) is linear in y, because curryLeft β is a continuous linear map.
- For y = τ_b, the (n+1)-tuple (τ_b, τ_0, …, τ_{n−1}) has equal entries at the distinct positions 0 and b+1. Since β is alternating, β vanishes on it.
- Hence the linear map vanishes on span(range τ) = Q (span induction over generators, 0, sums and scalar multiples). In particular it vanishes at y = x ∈ Q.

5. Conclusion. ξ(x)(ι_xβ) = ±(ι_xβ)(τ) = ±β(x, τ) = 0. As β was arbitrary, the conclusion holds at μ-a.e. x. The case n = 0 is included: then Q = span ∅ = {0} and x = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: μ ≪ Hⁿ⌞M transfers `orients` to μ-a.e. x.
Uniqueness of approximate tangent planes identifies approxTangentPlane with the oriented plane Q, and p_Q x = x gives x ∈ Q.
y ↦ β(y, τ) is linear and vanishes on each τ_b (repeated entry), hence on Q ∋ x.
Therefore ξ(x)(ι_xβ) = ±β(x, τ) = 0 for every β.

subproblems.title: Cartan's formula for the Euler field X(x) = x
subproblems.statement:
Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let β : ℝ^P → Λ^{m+1}(ℝ^P) be an (m+1)-form differentiable at y. Let ι_Xβ be the m-form z ↦ β(z).curryLeft z, the contraction with the Euler field X(z) = z. Then
 d(ι_Xβ)(y) + ι_y(dβ(y)) = (m+1)·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y].
This is Cartan's formula L_X = dι_X + ι_X d for X(z) = z, with d the exterior derivative (Mathlib extDeriv), ι_y(dβ(y)) = (dβ(y)).curryLeft y, and Dβ(y) the Fréchet derivative.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) (y : Euclid P), DifferentiableAt ℝ β y → exteriorDerivative (fun z => ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (β z) z) y + ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (exteriorDerivative β y) y = ((m : ℝ) + 1) • β y + fderiv ℝ β y y
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (not part of the proof): this is the comparator-accepted DAG node `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.euler_cartan-a1` (status accepted, candidate commit 77ba67182967, isolated comparator passed) with a byte-identical frozen type, so the controller attaches it and creates no new work. The numbered proof below is that node's frozen parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim from its parent-child-handoff.json without the Lean implementation note. In it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1` (constant density ratio implies cone, Simon 7.3.1), and 'sibling K' names the sibling with key K here. Role here: Cartan's formula d(ι_Xβ) + ι_X dβ = (m+1)β + Dβ[·] in step 4. It is used by lie_annihilation.

Source. This is the Cartan formula behind Simon's homotopy formula (Ch. 6, 2.25–2.26, chapter-06.txt lines 441–456) and Lemma 2.33 (lines 557–567), in the form used in step 6 of the parent proof: L_Xβ = d(ι_Xβ) + ι_X dβ for X(x) = x, where L_Xβ(y) = (m+1)β(y) + Dβ(y)[y] for an (m+1)-form β.

Conventions (Mathlib).
- dω(x) = alternatizeUncurryFin(Dω(x)).
- alt := alternatizeUncurryFin satisfies (alt f)(v_0, …, v_k) = Σ_{i=0}^{k} (−1)^i f(v_i)(v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_k).
- (f.curryLeft x)(v) = f(x, v).
Let B := Dβ(y) = fderiv ℝ β y : ℝ^P →L Λ^{m+1}, and ψ(z) := β(z).curryLeft z.

1. Derivative of ψ. Φ(f, z) := f.curryLeft z is continuous and bilinear, since curryLeft is a linear isometry Λ^{m+1} → L(ℝ^P, Λ^m). Since ψ(z) = Φ(β(z), z) and β is differentiable at y, the product rule gives Dψ(y)[u] = (Bu).curryLeft y + β(y).curryLeft u. That is, Dψ(y) = K + β(y).curryLeft with K(u) := (Bu).curryLeft y.

2. dψ(y). By additivity of alt, dψ(y) = alt(Dψ(y)) = alt(K) + alt(β(y).curryLeft) = A + (m+1)β(y).
- Here A := alt(K), so A(v) = Σ_{i=0}^{m} (−1)^i (Bv_i)(y, v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_m).
- alt(f.curryLeft) = (m+1)f because Σ_i (−1)^i f(v_i, v_0, …, v̂_i, …) = Σ_i f(v): moving the i-th entry to the front is a cyclic permutation of sign (−1)^i (Mathlib alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft).

3. ι_y dβ(y). Let v = (v_0, …, v_m) and w := (y, v_0, …, v_m). Then dβ(y)(w) = Σ_{k=0}^{m+1} (−1)^k B(w_k)(w with w_k removed).
- The k = 0 term is B(y)(v).
- For k = i+1, removing entry i+1 of (y, v) leaves (y, v without v_i), so the term is (−1)^{i+1}(Bv_i)(y, v_0, …, v̂_i, …, v_m).
Hence (dβ(y)).curryLeft y = B(y) − A.

4. Conclusion. Adding steps 2 and 3: dψ(y) + (dβ(y)).curryLeft y = A + (m+1)β(y) + B(y) − A = (m+1)·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y]. ∎
proof_key_steps: Product rule: Dψ(y)u = (Dβ(y)u).curryLeft y + β(y).curryLeft u for ψ(z) = β(z).curryLeft z.
dψ(y) = alt(u ↦ (Dβ(y)u).curryLeft y) + (m+1)β(y), by alternatizeUncurryFin_curryLeft.
(dβ(y)).curryLeft y = Dβ(y)y − alt(u ↦ (Dβ(y)u).curryLeft y), by splitting off the k = 0 term.
Adding: d(ι_Xβ)(y) + ι_y dβ(y) = (m+1)β(y) + Dβ(y)[y].

subproblems.title: Cone criterion: invariance of C under the dilation pull-backs ω ↦ λ⁻ⁿω(λ⁻¹·) gives IsConeCurrent C (unfolding η_{0,λ#})
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and let C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) be a current on all of ℝ^P (GeometricCurrentOn univ n). Assume that for every λ > 0 and all test forms ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with ω'(y) = λ^{−n}·ω(λ^{−1}y) for every y ∈ ℝ^P, one has C(ω') = C(ω). Then C is a cone (IsConeCurrent C): currentEval(η_{0,λ#}C, ω) = C(ω) for every λ > 0 and every ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P), where η_{0,λ#}C = blowUp C 0 λ is the push-forward of C by the dilation η_{0,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹y (Simon 6.2.23).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), (∀ lam : ℝ, 0 < lam → ∀ ω ω' : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, (∀ y, (ω' : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (lam⁻¹ ^ n) • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (lam⁻¹ • y)) → C ω' = C ω) → IsConeCurrent C
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (not part of the proof): this is the comparator-accepted DAG node `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1.cone_criterion-a1` (status accepted, candidate commit d120e82c5f33, isolated comparator passed) with a byte-identical frozen type, so the controller attaches it and creates no new work. In it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1` (the wedge-form cone criterion, Simon Lemma 6.2.33), and 'sibling K' names the sibling with key K here. Role here: step 1, the reduction of currentEval(blowUp S 0 λ, ω) to S(ω^λ) with ω^λ(y) = λ^{−n}ω(λ^{−1}y), and the last sentence of step 5.

Source. Step 7 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 2.23 for the proper affine map η_{0,λ}(y) = λ⁻¹y; Simon 7.3.1(2) "η_{0,λ#}C = C"). Contract definitions used: currentEval, blowUp, dilation, dilationCLM, IsConeCurrent. SimonGMT definitions used: GeometricCurrentOn.affinePushforward, affinePullbackTestOn, affinePullbackForm, GeometricCurrentOn.restrictDomain, testFormOnInclusion. The hypothesis is the parent's endpoint identity C(β_1) = C(ω) with β_1(y) = ω(λ⁻¹y)∘(λ⁻¹·) = λ⁻ⁿω(λ⁻¹y).

1. Goal. By definition IsConeCurrent C means: for every λ > 0 and every ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n, currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω). Fix λ > 0 and ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
2. The test-form branch of currentEval. The dilation η := dilation 0 λ is y ↦ −(λ⁻¹·0) + dilationCLM P λ y = λ⁻¹y.
- η is onto: for x ∈ ℝ^P, η(λx) = λ⁻¹(λx) = x because λ ≠ 0. Hence η '' univ = univ and tsupport ω ⊆ η '' univ.
- ω is a test form (C^∞ with compact support) because ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
So the condition of the `if` in currentEval holds, and currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = (blowUp C 0 λ)(⟨ω, h⟩). Here h records these two facts and ⟨ω, h⟩ ∈ TestFormOn (η '' univ) n.
3. Unfolding blowUp. By the contract, blowUp C 0 λ = (C.restrictDomain h₁).affinePushforward L b hp, where:
- L := dilationCLM P λ = λ⁻¹·id and b := −(λ⁻¹·0);
- h₁ is the inclusion (y ↦ b + Ly)⁻¹'(η '' univ) ⊆ univ;
- hp is the properness of y ↦ b + Ly.
By affinePushforward_apply and restrictDomain_apply (both hold by definition), (blowUp C 0 λ)(⟨ω, h⟩) = C(ω''). Here ω'' := testFormOnInclusion h₁ n (affinePullbackTestOn L b hp (η '' univ) n ⟨ω, h⟩) ∈ TestFormOn univ n is the test form whose underlying form is affinePullbackForm L b ω, i.e. ω''(y) = (ω(b + Ly)).compContinuousLinearMap L.
4. Computing ω''. Here b = 0 and Ly = λ⁻¹y. For y ∈ ℝ^P and v = (v_1, …, v_n):
ω''(y)(v_1, …, v_n) = ω(λ⁻¹y)(λ⁻¹v_1, …, λ⁻¹v_n) = (∏_{i=1}^n λ⁻¹)·ω(λ⁻¹y)(v_1, …, v_n) = (λ⁻¹)ⁿ·ω(λ⁻¹y)(v).
This is multilinearity of the alternating map ω(λ⁻¹y), one factor λ⁻¹ per slot (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.map_smul_univ, Finset.prod_const, card(Fin n) = n). Hence ω''(y) = (λ⁻¹)ⁿ • ω(λ⁻¹ • y) for every y (for n = 0 both sides are ω(λ⁻¹y)).
5. Applying the hypothesis. By step 4 the test forms ω and ω'' ∈ TestFormOn univ n satisfy the relation of the hypothesis for this λ > 0, so C(ω'') = C(ω).
6. Conclusion. By steps 2, 3 and 5, currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) = C(ω'') = C(ω). Since λ > 0 and ω were arbitrary, IsConeCurrent C. ∎
proof_key_steps: η_{0,λ} is onto, so currentEval(blowUp C 0 λ, ω) takes its test-form branch.
By definition of blowUp, affinePushforward and restrictDomain, η_{0,λ#}C(ω) = C(ω'') with ω''(y) = ω(λ⁻¹y)∘(λ⁻¹·id).
Multilinearity: ω''(y) = λ⁻ⁿω(λ⁻¹y).
The hypothesis gives C(ω'') = C(ω); hence IsConeCurrent C.

subproblems.title: Contraction with the Euler field preserves test forms
subproblems.statement: Let P, m ∈ ℕ and let β : ℝ^P → Λ^{m+1}(ℝ^P) (DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)) be a test form (IsTestForm β: C^∞ with compact support). Then the contraction of β with the Euler field X(z) = z, ι_Xβ : z ↦ β(z).curryLeft z (so (ι_Xβ)(z)(v_1, …, v_m) = β(z)(z, v_1, …, v_m)), is a test m-form: IsTestForm (fun z => ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (β z) z).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) (m + 1)), IsTestForm β → IsTestForm (fun z => ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft (β z) z)

In it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1` (the wedge-form cone criterion, Simon Lemma 6.2.33), and 'sibling K' names the sibling with key K here. Role here: the facts in step 4 that ι_Xβ_s and ι_X dβ_s are test forms. It is used by lie_annihilation.

Source. Step 4 of the parent proof ("Both are smooth (compositions of smooth maps with continuous bilinear maps …) and have tsupport ⊆ tsupport β_{s₀}"), used there for ψ = ι_Xβ and χ = ι_X dβ (Simon Ch. 6, 2.25–2.26 and Lemma 2.33).
- Conventions: (f.curryLeft x)(v_1, …, v_m) = f(x, v_1, …, v_m) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft).
- IsTestForm φ means φ is C^∞ (all orders, ContDiff ℝ ∞) and has compact support.

1. Bilinear structure. f ↦ f.curryLeft is a linear isometry Λ^{m+1}(ℝ^P) → L(ℝ^P, Λ^m(ℝ^P)) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeftLI); write A for it as a continuous linear map. Then (ι_Xβ)(z) = A(β(z))(z) for every z.
2. Smoothness. z ↦ A(β(z)) is C^∞ (a continuous linear map composed with the C^∞ map β), and z ↦ z is C^∞. The application of a C^∞ family of continuous linear maps to a C^∞ vector is C^∞ (Mathlib ContDiff.clm_apply). Hence ι_Xβ is C^∞.
3. Support. If β(z) = 0, then (ι_Xβ)(z) = 0.curryLeft z = 0. Hence supp(ι_Xβ) ⊆ supp β ⊆ tsupport β, which is compact since β has compact support; therefore ι_Xβ has compact support (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.mono).
4. By steps 2 and 3, ι_Xβ is a test m-form. ∎
proof_key_steps: ι_Xβ(z) = A(β(z))(z) with A = curryLeftLI, a continuous linear map.
C^∞: a C^∞ family of continuous linear maps applied to the C^∞ vector z (ContDiff.clm_apply).
β(z) = 0 ⇒ ι_Xβ(z) = 0, so supp ι_Xβ ⊆ tsupport β is compact (HasCompactSupport.mono).

subproblems.title: Differentiation under the integral sign for the dilation family s ↦ τ(M,θ,ξ)(sⁿω(s·))
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ, let R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) be an integer multiplicity triple in ℝ^P (M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient), let ω ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) and t > 0. For s ∈ ℝ put G(s) := R.action(y ↦ sⁿ·ω(s·y)) = ∫_M θ(y)·ξ(y)(sⁿω(sy)) dHⁿ(y). Then G has derivative at t equal to R.action(y ↦ n·t^{n−1}·ω(t·y) + tⁿ·Dω(t·y)[y]), where Dω(z)[u] = fderiv ℝ ω z u and n·t^{n−1} means (n : ℝ)·t^{n−1} with natural-number exponent n − 1 (so this coefficient is 0 when n = 0).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (ω : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → HasDerivAt (fun s : ℝ => R.action (fun y => (s ^ n) • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (s • y))) (R.action (fun y => ((n : ℝ) * t ^ (n - 1)) • (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (t • y) + (t ^ n) • fderiv ℝ (ω : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) (t • y) y)) t
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (not part of the proof): this is the comparator-accepted DAG node `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1.scaled_derivative-a1` (status accepted, candidate commit 81f1c23cd960, isolated comparator passed) with a byte-identical frozen type, so the controller attaches it and creates no new work. The numbered proof below is that node's frozen parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim from its parent-child-handoff.json without the Lean implementation note. In it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1` (the wedge-form cone criterion, Simon Lemma 6.2.33), and 'sibling K' names the sibling with key K here. Role here: step 3, the differentiation of G(s) = R.action(s^nω(s·)) under the integral sign. It is used by dilation_invariance.

Source. Steps 0(a), 0(b), 2 and 3 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 2.33 via the homotopy formula 2.25–2.27, chapter-06.txt lines 441–478 and 557–567).
- Specialization: the identity parametrization c(s) = s on J = (0, ∞), i.e. β_s(y) = sⁿω(sy) = h_s^#ω for h_s(y) = sy. The parent's Remark records that any smooth positive parametrization works verbatim; here c' ≡ 1.
- Notation: M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M. Thus R.action φ = ∫ θ(y)·ξ(y)(φ(y)) dν(y) for every form φ.
- Dω(z) = fderiv ℝ ω z; norms on Covector (Euclid P) n and MultiVector P n are operator norms.

1. Orientation bound (parent 0(a)). By R.orients, for ν-a.e. y there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(y)) Q; by the sibling orientation_norm, ‖ξ(y)‖ ≤ 1. Hence for ν-a.e. y and every covector α: |ξ(y)(α)| ≤ ‖ξ(y)‖·‖α‖ ≤ ‖α‖.
2. Data from ω. ω ∈ TestFormOn univ n is C^∞ with compact support.
- ω and Dω are continuous.
- ω(z) = 0 and Dω(z) = 0 whenever z ∉ tsupport ω, since tsupport(Dω) ⊆ tsupport ω (Mathlib tsupport_fderiv_subset).
- Choose r ∈ ℝ with tsupport ω ⊆ B̄_r(0) (a compact set is bounded).
- Choose K₀ with ‖ω(z)‖ ≤ K₀ for all z (continuous with compact support); then K₀ ≥ ‖ω(0)‖ ≥ 0.
3. Integrands. For s ∈ ℝ and y ∈ ℝ^P put
- Φ(s, y) := n·s^{n−1}·ω(sy) + sⁿ·Dω(sy)[y],
- F(s, y) := θ(y)·ξ(y)(sⁿω(sy)),
- F'(s, y) := θ(y)·ξ(y)(Φ(s, y)).
Then G(s) = ∫ F(s, ·) dν, and the claimed derivative is ∫ F'(t, ·) dν = R.action(y ↦ Φ(t, y)).
4. Pointwise derivative (parent step 2 with c(s) = s). Fix y.
- s ↦ sy has derivative y.
- By the chain rule, s ↦ ω(sy) has derivative Dω(sy)[y] (ω is differentiable).
- s ↦ sⁿ has derivative n·s^{n−1} (Mathlib hasDerivAt_pow, coefficient (n : ℝ)·s^{n−1}).
- By the product rule, s ↦ sⁿω(sy) has derivative sⁿ·Dω(sy)[y] + n·s^{n−1}·ω(sy) = Φ(s, y).
Composing with the continuous linear functional ξ(y) and multiplying by the constant θ(y), s ↦ F(s, y) has derivative F'(s, y) at every s, for every y.
5. Measurability.
- θ is measurable (R.measurable_mult composed with ℕ → ℝ), and ξ is AEStronglyMeasurable for ν (R.aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
- (s, y) ↦ Φ(s, y) is jointly continuous: ω, Dω, the evaluation (A, u) ↦ A u, scalar multiplication and powers are continuous. Also y ↦ sⁿω(sy) is continuous.
- The evaluation (ζ, α) ↦ ζ(α) is continuous on MultiVector P n × Covector (Euclid P) n, so y ↦ ξ(y)(φ(y)) is AEStronglyMeasurable for every continuous φ.
- Multiplying by θ(y), F(s, ·) (each s) and F'(t, ·) are AEStronglyMeasurable for ν.
6. Localization. Let I := (t/2, 2t), an open neighbourhood of t, ρ := 2r/t and B := B̄_ρ(0) (compact, measurable).
- If s ∈ I and sy ∈ tsupport ω, then s‖y‖ = ‖sy‖ ≤ r, so r ≥ 0 and ‖y‖ ≤ r/s ≤ 2r/t = ρ, i.e. y ∈ B.
- If sy ∉ tsupport ω, then ω(sy) = 0 and Dω(sy) = 0 by step 2, so sⁿω(sy) = 0, Φ(s, y) = 0 and F(s, y) = F'(s, y) = 0.
7. Uniform bound (parent step 3). Φ is continuous on the compact set [t/2, 2t] × B, so there is K with ‖Φ(s, y)‖ ≤ K for (s, y) ∈ [t/2, 2t] × B. One may take the parent's explicit constant K = n(2t)^{n−1}K₀ + (2t)ⁿ·sup‖Dω‖·ρ (i.e. M₀ = 2t, m₀ = t/2, |c'| = 1).
Let g(y) := K·θ(y)·1_B(y). For ν-a.e. y (those of step 1) and every s ∈ I:
- if sy ∈ tsupport ω, then y ∈ B by step 6 and |F'(s, y)| ≤ θ(y)·‖ξ(y)‖·‖Φ(s, y)‖ ≤ θ(y)·1·K = g(y);
- otherwise F'(s, y) = 0 ≤ g(y): g(y) = 0 if y ∉ B, and if y ∈ B then K ≥ ‖Φ(t, y)‖ ≥ 0 since (t, y) ∈ [t/2, 2t] × B.
8. Integrability (parent 0(b)).
- B is compact and B ⊆ univ, so R.locallyIntegrable_mult gives ∫_{M∩B} θ dHⁿ < ∞. As θ is measurable, θ·1_B is ν-integrable, hence so is g.
- By step 6 with s = t ∈ I and step 1, |F(t, y)| ≤ tⁿK₀·θ(y)·1_B(y) for ν-a.e. y. Indeed, if ty ∈ tsupport ω then y ∈ B and |F(t, y)| ≤ θ(y)·‖tⁿω(ty)‖ ≤ tⁿK₀θ(y); otherwise F(t, y) = 0 and the right side is ≥ 0. So F(t, ·) is ν-integrable.
9. Conclusion. The dominated differentiation theorem (Mathlib hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le) applies with the neighbourhood I of t:
- F(s, ·) is AEStronglyMeasurable for s near t (step 5);
- F(t, ·) is integrable (step 8);
- F'(t, ·) is AEStronglyMeasurable (step 5);
- |F'(s, y)| ≤ g(y) for ν-a.e. y and all s ∈ I, with g integrable (steps 7–8);
- s ↦ F(s, y) has derivative F'(s, y) on I for every y (step 4).
Hence G(s) = ∫ F(s, ·) dν has derivative ∫ F'(t, ·) dν = R.action(y ↦ n·t^{n−1}·ω(ty) + tⁿ·Dω(ty)[y]) at t. ∎
proof_key_steps: ‖ξ(y)‖ ≤ 1 for Hⁿ⌞M-a.e. y (orientation_norm via R.orients).
For every y, s ↦ θ(y)ξ(y)(sⁿω(sy)) has derivative θ(y)ξ(y)(n s^{n−1}ω(sy) + sⁿDω(sy)[y]) (product and chain rules).
For s ∈ (t/2, 2t) the integrands vanish unless y ∈ B̄_{2r/t}(0) (tsupport ω ⊆ B̄_r(0)), and are bounded by Kθ(y)1_B(y) with K the maximum of the continuous Φ on [t/2, 2t] × B.
θ1_B is integrable by locallyIntegrable_mult; the integrands are AEStronglyMeasurable.
hasDerivAt_integral_of_dominated_loc_of_deriv_le gives G'(t) = R.action(n t^{n−1}ω(t·) + tⁿDω(t·)[·]).

subproblems.title: ∂C = 0 and x ∧ C⃗ = 0 a.e. imply that C annihilates Euler–Lie derivatives of test forms (core of Simon 6.2.33)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ with n ≥ 1, C ∈ 𝒟_n(ℝ^P) (GeometricCurrentOn univ n) and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n) with C = τ(M, θ, ξ) (R.Represents C). Assume ∂C = 0 (BoundaryVanishes C) and x ∧ C⃗ = 0 μ_C-a.e. in the sense that for R.measure-a.e. x, ξ(x)(α.curryLeft x) = 0 for every (n+1)-covector α. Then C(γ) = 0 for all test forms β, γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) with γ(y) = n·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y] for every y (Dβ(y) = fderiv ℝ β y); that is, C annihilates the Lie derivative L_Xβ = d(ι_Xβ) + ι_X dβ of every test form along the Euler field X(y) = y.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (C : GeometricCurrentOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n) (R : IMRep (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n), 0 < n → R.Represents C → BoundaryVanishes C → (∀ᵐ x ∂R.measure, ∀ β : Covector (Euclid P) (n + 1), R.orient x (ContinuousAlternatingMap.curryLeft β x) = 0) → ∀ β γ : TestFormOn (univ : Set (Euclid P)) n, (∀ y, (γ : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y = (n : ℝ) • (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y + fderiv ℝ (β : DifferentialForm (Euclid P) n) y y) → C γ = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Reuse note (not part of the proof): this is the comparator-accepted DAG node `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1.lie_annihilation-a1` (status accepted, candidate commit dd88db759fe2, isolated comparator passed) with a byte-identical frozen type, so the controller attaches it and creates no new work. The numbered proof below is that node's frozen parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim from its parent-child-handoff.json without the Lean implementation note. In it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1` (the wedge-form cone criterion, Simon Lemma 6.2.33), and 'sibling K' names the sibling with key K here. Role here: step 4: S(γ) = 0 for every Euler–Lie derivative γ = nβ + Dβ[·] of a test form β, from ∂S = 0 and the wedge vanishing of step 2.

Source. Steps 0(c), 0(d), 4 and 5 of the parent proof.
- Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 2.33 (chapter-06.txt lines 557–567): its proof shows that the homotopy term vanishes because x ∧ C⃗ = 0 and ∂C = 0. Here this is made explicit through Cartan's formula L_X = dι_X + ι_X d for the Euler field X(x) = x.
- Simon 7.3.1 (chapter-07.txt line 359) applies the lemma to tangent cones.
Notation:
- M = R.carrier, θ = R.mult, ξ = R.orient, ν := Hⁿ⌞M = μHE[n].restrict M, and R.measure = ν.withDensity θ.
- R.Represents C means C(φ) = R.action(φ) = ∫ θ(y)ξ(y)(φ(y)) dν(y) for all φ ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
- ι_Xφ(z) := φ(z).curryLeft z; d = exteriorDerivative; Dβ(y) = fderiv ℝ β y.

1. Since n ≥ 1, write n = m + 1. Then (n : ℝ) = m + 1, the wedge hypothesis concerns (m+2)-covectors, and BoundaryVanishes C means C.boundary = 0 (definition of BoundaryVanishes in degree m + 1).
2. ψ := ι_Xβ is a test m-form. β is a test (m+1)-form, so by the sibling contraction_test_form, z ↦ β(z).curryLeft z is C^∞ with compact support. Regard it as ψ ∈ TestFormOn univ m (tsupport ⊆ univ).
3. χ := ι_X dβ is a test (m+1)-form. dβ is a test (m+2)-form, since exterior differentiation preserves test forms (SimonGMT exteriorDerivative_isTestForm). So by contraction_test_form applied with m + 1 in place of m, χ(z) = (dβ(z)).curryLeft z defines χ ∈ TestFormOn univ (m+1).
4. Cartan. β is C^∞, hence differentiable at every y, so the sibling euler_cartan gives dψ(y) + χ(y) = (m+1)·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y] = γ(y) for every y (hypothesis on γ, with (n : ℝ) = m + 1). Hence γ = dψ + χ in TestFormOn univ (m+1), where dψ = exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ψ.
5. Linearity (parent 0(d)). C is linear on test forms, so C(γ) = C(dψ) + C(χ).
6. Boundary term (parent 0(d), step 5). By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, C(dψ) = C(exteriorDerivativeTestOn univ m ψ) = (C.boundary)(ψ) = 0, since C.boundary = 0.
7. Wedge term (parent 0(c), step 5). C(χ) = R.action(χ) = ∫ θ(y)·ξ(y)((dβ(y)).curryLeft y) dν(y).
- The function y ↦ (θ(y) : ℝ≥0∞) is measurable. By Mathlib ae_withDensity_iff, the hypothesis "for R.measure-a.e. x, ξ(x)(α.curryLeft x) = 0 for all α" is equivalent to: for ν-a.e. y, θ(y) ≠ 0 implies ξ(y)(α.curryLeft y) = 0 for all α.
- ν-a.e. y lies in M (ν is Hⁿ restricted to the measurable set M), and θ(y) > 0 for y ∈ M (R.mult_pos).
- Taking α := dβ(y), the integrand θ(y)·ξ(y)((dβ(y)).curryLeft y) vanishes for ν-a.e. y, so the integral is 0 (no integrability needed).
Thus C(χ) = 0.
8. Conclusion. C(γ) = C(dψ) + C(χ) = 0 + 0 = 0. ∎
proof_key_steps: n = m + 1; ψ := ι_Xβ ∈ 𝒟^m and χ := ι_X dβ ∈ 𝒟^{m+1} by contraction_test_form (dβ is a test form).
euler_cartan: dψ + χ = (m+1)β + Dβ[·] = γ, so C(γ) = C(dψ) + C(χ).
C(dψ) = (∂C)(ψ) = 0 since ∂C = 0.
C(χ) = ∫_M θ ξ((dβ(y)).curryLeft y) dHⁿ = 0: the wedge hypothesis transfers from θHⁿ⌞M to Hⁿ⌞M (ae_withDensity_iff, θ ≥ 1 on M).

subproblems.title: Annihilation of Euler–Lie derivatives makes τ(M,θ,ξ) invariant under the dilation pull-backs (homotopy constancy)
subproblems.statement: Let P, n ∈ ℕ and R = (M, θ, ξ) ∈ IMRep(ℝ^P, n). Assume that R.action(γ) = 0 for all test forms β, γ ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) (TestFormOn univ n) satisfying γ(y) = n·β(y) + Dβ(y)[y] for every y (γ is the Lie derivative of β along the Euler field X(y) = y; Dβ(y) = fderiv ℝ β y). Then for every λ > 0 and all ω, ω' ∈ 𝒟ⁿ(ℝ^P) with ω'(y) = λ^{−n}·ω(λ^{−1}y) for every y, R.action(ω') = R.action(ω).

Reuse note (not part of the proof): this is the comparator-accepted DAG node `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1.dilation_invariance-a1` (status accepted, candidate commit da8da23e49ee, isolated comparator passed) with a byte-identical frozen type, so the controller attaches it and creates no new work. The numbered proof below is that node's frozen parent-supplied proof, copied verbatim from its parent-child-handoff.json without the Lean implementation note. In it, 'the parent proof' means the proof of `root.density_and_tangent_cones-a1.cone-a1.cone_lemma-a1` (the wedge-form cone criterion, Simon Lemma 6.2.33), and 'sibling K' names the sibling with key K here. Role here: the identity sG'(s) = S(γ_s) of step 3 and step 5: G is constant on (0, ∞), so R.action(ω^λ) = R.action(ω).

Source. Steps 1, 2 (the identity ∂_sβ_s = (c'/c(s))·Lβ_s), 4 (Lβ_s is a test form) and 6 (constancy) of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, Lemma 2.33 via the homotopy formula 2.25–2.27).
- Specialization: the identity parametrization c(s) = s on J = (0, ∞), which the parent's Remark allows. Thus β_s(y) := sⁿω(sy) = h_s^#ω for h_s(y) = sy, so β_1 = ω, β_{λ⁻¹}(y) = λ⁻ⁿω(λ⁻¹y) (the parent's β_1) and c'/c(s) = 1/s.
- Notation: Dφ(y) = fderiv ℝ φ y; Lβ(y) := nβ(y) + Dβ(y)[y].

1. The function G. For s ∈ ℝ let β_s(y) := sⁿ·ω(sy) and G(s) := R.action(β_s).
- G(1) = R.action(ω), since 1ⁿ = 1 and 1·y = y.
- G(λ⁻¹) = R.action(ω'), since β_{λ⁻¹}(y) = (λ⁻¹)ⁿ·ω(λ⁻¹y) = ω'(y) for every y by hypothesis.
2. Constant factors. For c ∈ ℝ and any form φ, R.action(y ↦ c·φ(y)) = c·R.action(φ). Indeed θ(y)·ξ(y)(c·φ(y)) = c·(θ(y)·ξ(y)(φ(y))) by linearity of ξ(y), and ∫ c·f = c·∫ f (no integrability needed).
3. β_t is a test form for t ≠ 0.
- It is C^∞: ω is C^∞, y ↦ ty is linear, and the constant factor is tⁿ.
- Its support lies in the support of y ↦ ω(ty), because β_t(y) ≠ 0 forces ω(ty) ≠ 0. That support is compact since y ↦ ty is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P for t ≠ 0 (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.comp_smul).
Hence β_t ∈ TestFormOn univ n (tsupport ⊆ univ trivially).
4. Chain rule. Dβ_t(y) = tⁿ·(Dω(ty)∘(t·id)), so Dβ_t(y)[y] = tⁿ·Dω(ty)[ty] = tⁿ⁺¹·Dω(ty)[y].
5. γ_t := Lβ_t is a test form for t ≠ 0, and R.action(γ_t) = 0. Let γ_t(y) := n·β_t(y) + Dβ_t(y)[y].
- γ_t is C^∞: β_t is C^∞, hence so is Dβ_t, and applying a C^∞ family of continuous linear maps to the C^∞ vector y is C^∞ (Mathlib ContDiff.fderiv_right, ContDiff.clm_apply).
- Its support lies in supp β_t ∪ supp Dβ_t, and Dβ_t has compact support because β_t does (Mathlib HasCompactSupport.fderiv). So γ_t ∈ TestFormOn univ n.
- The pair (β_t, γ_t) satisfies γ_t(y) = n·β_t(y) + Dβ_t(y)[y] for all y by definition, so the hypothesis gives R.action(γ_t) = 0.
6. The derivative integrand is t⁻¹γ_t. Fix t > 0. By step 4,
γ_t(y) = n·tⁿ·ω(ty) + tⁿ⁺¹·Dω(ty)[y] = t·(n·t^{n−1}·ω(ty) + tⁿ·Dω(ty)[y]).
(For n ≥ 1, t·t^{n−1} = tⁿ; for n = 0 both first terms are 0.) Hence y ↦ n·t^{n−1}·ω(ty) + tⁿ·Dω(ty)[y] is the form y ↦ t⁻¹·γ_t(y), and by step 2 its action is t⁻¹·R.action(γ_t) = 0.
7. G' = 0 on (0, ∞). By the sibling scaled_derivative, for every t > 0, G has derivative R.action(y ↦ n·t^{n−1}·ω(ty) + tⁿ·Dω(ty)[y]) at t, which is 0 by step 6. This is the parent's F'(s₀) = (c'/c(s₀))·R.action(Lβ_{s₀}) = 0 with c(s) = s. So G is differentiable on the open interval (0, ∞) with derivative 0 there.
8. Constancy (parent step 6). (0, ∞) is open and connected (convex), so by the mean value theorem G is constant on it (Mathlib IsOpen.is_const_of_deriv_eq_zero). Since λ⁻¹ > 0 and 1 > 0, step 1 gives R.action(ω') = G(λ⁻¹) = G(1) = R.action(ω). ∎
proof_key_steps: G(s) := R.action(β_s), β_s(y) = sⁿω(sy); G(1) = R.action ω and G(λ⁻¹) = R.action ω'.
For t > 0, β_t and γ_t := nβ_t + Dβ_t[·] are test forms, so R.action γ_t = 0 by hypothesis.
Chain rule Dβ_t(y)[y] = tⁿ⁺¹Dω(ty)[y] gives n t^{n−1}ω(ty) + tⁿDω(ty)[y] = t⁻¹γ_t(y).
scaled_derivative: G'(t) = R.action(t⁻¹γ_t) = t⁻¹R.action γ_t = 0 on (0, ∞).
Mean value theorem on the connected open set (0, ∞): G(λ⁻¹) = G(1).
